text:
amanda_sales: Looping folks in — Acme wants a 4-week POC to validate our assistant for their support flows. High level: ~2k DAU, expected 3k sessions/day, avg 150 tokens per response, spike factor 4 during business hours. Success criteria they care about: p95 latency < 250ms, retained answer accuracy >= 88% on their eval set, and spend <= $5k over the trial.

mike_se: Thanks. Need to confirm a couple things: is 3k sessions/day the total (incl retries), and do they expect streaming responses or full-response generation? Streaming affects latency but not token cost.

amanda_sales: 3k is net successful sessions. They'll do retry on failure but small. Streaming preferred for UX but not required.

julia_sre: For p95 <250ms with streaming we should assume single-turn median seq len 150, but worst-case 2k tokens for long context (rare). With spike factor 4 that implies peak concurrent RPS ~= (3k sessions/day * 4) / (3600*peak_hours_fraction). Can you confirm peak concentration?

raj_ml: Quick back-of-envelope: 3k sessions/day -> avg 0.035 rps overall. If 60% of traffic hits in 4 hours -> peak ~0.5 rps. With spike factor 4 -> ~2 rps. For 150 tokens response, that's 300 tokens/sec generated at 2 rps if each request takes ~0.5s to stream. For model throughput estimates: an A100-80GB int8/4-bit quantized LLM can sustain ~400-800 tokens/s for single-stream generation depending on model. So one GPU could handle this comfortably for the POC with low latency.

mike_se: Good. For safety I'd recommend 1 dedicated GPU (burst to a second) with autoscale policy enabled on Dedicated or equivalent in Hosted. That keeps cost down but meets latency SLO.

emma_ps: Pricing check: if we run hosted and bill per token, rough token cost assumption $0.0003 per token (example) -> 3k sessions * 150 tokens * 30 days = 13.5M tokens -> cost ~$4k. Add infra/overhead & margin -> hits their $5k cap but tight. If we need extra headroom for eval runs, might go over.

amanda_sales: They will run internal evals ~10k eval prompts during week 1. Add that in?

raj_ml: Add 10k * 150 = 1.5M tokens -> +$450 at that token rate. Still within budget but less buffer. Recommend we propose two options: a) Hosted single-GPU equivalent with token billing cap at $6k (recommended), b) Dedicated 1 GPU with burst to 2 GPUs for a flat weekly fee (we need ops to price).

julia_sre: Operational asks: enable KV/prefix caching for repeated system prompts, set request timeout 5s, circuit breaker to fallback to smaller model variant if latency spikes. Also we need to instrument per-prompt eval hooks (send copies to their eval pipeline).

amanda_sales: Client also asked about security question: can we sign an NDA + support SOC2 in 30 days? They need audit logs for the POC.

emma_ps: NDA yes. SOC2 we provide artifacts but not a full attestation in 30 days; we can offer enhanced logging (redwood-console retention increase) for the POC as a compromise. I'll ack and follow up with legal.

ops_bot: ticket#4521 created: "Acme POC — capacity + pricing + eval hooks". Assigned: julia_sre, raj_ml, mike_se.

mike_se: Next steps: (1) send concise SOW with traffic assumptions and two pricing options, (2) schedule 30-min ops sync to confirm autoscale and caching configs, (3) provide sample cost calc and expected p95 latency numbers. I can draft SOW.

amanda_sales: Perfect. I'll loop in the Acme procurement and legal after we have SOW. ETA for SOW draft: EOD tomorrow.

raj_ml: Note for SOW: include a runbook snippet for long-tail requests that triggers a model-variant fallback (e.g., smaller LM for >1000 token gen) and estimation table: "expected tokens/day", "peak RPS", "recommended GPU".

amanda_sales: Great — thanks everyone.

mike_se: tagging @emma_ps and @julia_sre — please confirm pricing assumptions and whether we can offer a 10% experimental credit for eval traffic by EOD.

emma_ps: Confirmed I'll check numbers and reply by 16:00 PST.

julia_sre: I'll prepare the autoscale config + caching notes and post a snippet in the ops sync.

amanda_sales: Closing loop — will post Acme's official numbers when received. :thumbsup:
